title: Equity Finance and Debt Finance Overview
statements: Share capital provided by outside investors is an external equity source of finance for the corporation.
Retained earnings that remain in the business count as internal equity finance under the standard overview.
Funds provided by investors are classified as external equity finance in the sources-of-finance framework.
Bank overdrafts and trade credit are commonly listed examples of short-term debt finance.
Long-term bank loans and bonds issued to investors are forms of long-term external debt finance.
context: Review the overview of sources of finance as classified into equity finance and debt finance. Evaluate the following economic assertions:

title: Internal and External Finance Classification
statements: Equity finance encompasses both internal sources such as retained earnings and external sources such as share capital.
Short-term bank loans used to cover working capital are classified as short-term debt finance.
Debt finance is always external because borrowed funds create obligations to outside creditors.
The balance sheet reveals the sources of finance that a business has used in building its assets.
Large businesses are obliged to draw up a balance sheet showing how operations have been funded.

title: Misclassifying Retained Earnings
statements: A loan provided by owners is classified as long-term credit within external debt finance.
Share capital is internal equity finance because issued shares are recorded on the corporation's own balance sheet.
Retained earnings are external equity because they ultimately derive from revenue paid by customers.
Debt finance is classified as internal finance because interest payments return profit to the owners.
Bank overdrafts are long-term debt finance because the overdraft limit may remain available for years.

title: Core Sources of Finance Definitions
statements: Bonds are short-term debt finance because holders may sell them quickly on secondary markets.
Trade credit from suppliers is short-term debt finance that postpones payment for goods and services.
Bonds issued to investors provide long-term debt finance through formal creditor instruments.
Long-term bank loans are a form of long-term external debt finance used for extended investment periods.
A loan provided by owners is equity finance because owners already participate in business ownership.

title: Short-Term Debt and Internal Equity
statements: Short-term and long-term credit from creditors are recorded as debt finance on the balance sheet.
Trade credit is equity finance because suppliers effectively share the commercial risk of the buyer.
Funds provided by investors are debt finance because investors expect a financial return.
Retained earnings are debt finance because they must eventually be repaid to creditors.
Equity finance includes share capital from investors and retained earnings kept within the firm.

title: Balance Sheet and Finance Sources
statements: Debt finance covers short-term credit such as overdrafts and long-term credit such as bank loans.
Funds provided by investors count as external equity when investors subscribe for ownership in the firm.
Retained earnings reinvested in the business represent internal equity finance rather than borrowed funds.
Short-term bank loans are short-term debt finance used to cover temporary funding gaps.
A loan provided by owners is long-term debt finance even though the lenders are also owners of the firm.

statements: Table 3 shows that debt finance is always external to the business entity.

title: Owner Loans Versus Share Capital
statements: Share capital is long-term debt finance because shareholders commit funds for many years.
Trade credit from suppliers is short-term external debt finance for purchases on deferred payment terms.
Short-term bank loans are long-term debt finance when the borrower intends to renew them repeatedly.
Debt finance can be internal when the lender is a shareholder who also receives dividend payments.
Share capital from investors is external equity finance contributing to the ownership base of the corporation.

title: Nuanced Debt and Equity Distinctions
statements: Retained earnings are external equity because they represent value generated from outside customer payments.
Bonds and long-term bank loans are long-term debt finance creating creditor claims on the firm.
Bank overdrafts are equity finance when used to cover working capital shortfalls.
Table 3 classifies retained earnings as short-term debt because they can be spent within one year.

title: Table 3 Finance Sources
statements: Debt finance is external and divided into short-term credit and long-term credit components.

Bank overdrafts, trade credit, and short-term loans exemplify short-term debt finance.

title: Single Correct Bond Classification
statements: Equity finance is always external because only shareholders provide it.

Bonds are short-term debt finance because coupon payments occur at regular intervals.
Share capital is external equity finance because investors contribute ownership funds from outside the business.

title: Trade Credit and Overdraft Traps
statements: Retained earnings are external equity because they arise from revenue paid by outside customers.
Bank overdrafts are short-term debt finance even when used repeatedly throughout the trading year.
Bank overdrafts are equity finance when the account holder is also a major shareholder of the bank.
A loan provided by owners is equity finance because the lenders share in the ownership of the business.

title: Investor Funds Classification
statements: Funds provided by investors are short-term debt finance when investors expect to exit within one reporting cycle.
Bonds issued to investors are long-term debt finance creating creditor claims traded in capital markets.
Debt finance includes internal sources when the firm repays loans using its own retained earnings.
Share capital is internal equity finance because share registers are maintained within the corporation's offices.
Retained earnings are external equity because they are disclosed in published financial statements.

title: Mixed Finance Source Assertions
statements: Share capital and funds from investors are external equity finance sources listed in the finance overview.

Bank overdrafts are long-term debt finance because banks review and maintain overdraft limits over time.
Bonds are long-term debt finance raising external creditor funds from investors.
Trade credit is short-term debt finance allowing suppliers to defer cash receipt for goods delivered.

title: Comprehensive Finance Source Review
statements: Long-term bank loans are long-term debt finance with repayment schedules extending beyond one year.
A loan provided by owners is long-term credit classified as external debt finance in the overview.
Short-term bank loans are short-term debt finance covering near-term working-capital requirements.
Equity finance includes both internal retained earnings and external share capital from investors.
